briefdescription.para: List of callbacks for globals being tracked by this analysis.

detaileddescription.para: Note that these objects are quite large, but we only anticipate having one per global tracked by this analysis. There are numerous optimizations we could perform to the memory utilization here if this becomes a problem.

briefdescription.para: Returns the function info for the function, or null if we don't have anything useful to say about it.
AnalyzeGlobals - Scan through the users of all of the internal GlobalValue's in the program.

detaileddescription.para: If none of them have their "address taken" (really, their address passed to something nontrivial), record this fact, and record the functions that they are used directly in.

briefdescription.para: AnalyzeCallGraph - At this point, we know the functions where globals are immediately stored to and read from.

detaileddescription.para: Propagate this information up the call graph to all callers and compute the mod/ref info for all memory for each function.

briefdescription.para: AnalyzeUsesOfPointer - Look at all of the users of the specified pointer.

detaileddescription.para: If this is used by anything complex (i.e., the address escapes), return true. Also, while we are at it, keep track of those functions that read and write to the value.
If OkayStoreDest is non-null, stores into this global are allowed.

briefdescription.para: AnalyzeIndirectGlobalMemory - We found an non-address-taken global variable which holds a pointer type.

detaileddescription.para: See if the global always points to non-aliased heap memory: that is, all initializers of the globals store a value known to be obtained via a noalias return function call which have no other use. Further, all loads out of GV must directly use the memory, not store the pointer somewhere. If this is true, we consider the memory pointed to by GV to be owned by GV and can disambiguate other pointers from it.
